title: Exodus Launches Zero Swap Fees on XRP for OneKey Users
summary: Limited-time campaign lets OneKey users swap into XRP with no XO Swap platform fees OMAHA, Neb., July 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Exodus…...
body_text: Exodus Launches Zero Swap Fees on XRP for OneKey Users July 07, 2026 4:30pm EDT Download as PDF Limited-time campaign lets OneKey users swap into XRP with no XO Swap platform fees OMAHA, Neb., July 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Exodus Movement, Inc. (NYSE American: EXOD) (“Exodus”) and Celestial Technology Ltd. (“OneKey”) today announced a limited-time campaign offering zero platform fees on inbound XRP swaps inside the OneKey app. During the promotion, OneKey users can swap into XRP from any supported asset through Exodus’ XO Swap cross-chain exchange aggregator with no platform fees. Standard network and gas fees will still apply. “XO Swap was built to make self-custody work wherever people choose to hold their assets,” said JP Richardson, CEO and Co-Founder of Exodus. “With OneKey, we’re removing platform fees on inbound XRP swaps so more customers can access XRP without giving up control of their assets.” "XRP is one of the most requested assets in our community,” said Niq Chen, Growth Lead at OneKey. “Partnering with Exodus to bring the swap fee to zero was a straightforward decision. Our holders want access, and now cost doesn’t stand in the way.” The promotion is available to all OneKey Wallet users through the swap interface inside the OneKey app. The campaign builds on the April 2026 expansion of native XRP Ledger (XRPL) and Ripple USD (RLUSD) support inside the Exodus wallet. XRP remains among the most actively swapped assets across the Exodus and XO Swap platforms by volume. About Exodus Movement, Inc. Founded in 2015, Exodus Movement, Inc. (NYSE American: EXOD) is pioneering self-custodial finance by giving people the tools to earn rewards, spend, manage, and swap digital assets across borders, all without giving up control. Exodus serves millions of consumers through its products built on a simple principle: your money should be yours. Exodus also powers crypto infrastructure for enterprise platforms serving millions of consumers through its enterprise product suite. Headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, Exodus builds financial software where control is the default. For more information, visit exodus.com. Investor Contact [email protected] Media Contacts Aubrey Strobel / Elena Nisonoff, Halcyon Communications [email protected] About OneKey Founded in 2019, OneKey is one of the world’s leading open-source app and hardware wallet brands. Its secure mobile app lets users trade crypto, US stocks, gold, crude oil, and more, while its hardware wallets feature advanced secure chips and top-tier security. Completely open source from day one, OneKey safeguards billions in digital assets. All code has passed rigorous audits by SlowMist and Offside Labs and is fully open-sourced on GitHub. Backed by Yzi Labs, Coinbase, and Dragonfly, OneKey is known for its exceptional security and quality. Media Contacts Niq Chen [email protected] Disclosure Information Exodus uses the following as means of disclosing material nonpublic information and for complying with disclosure obligations under Regulation FD: websites exodus.com/investors and exodus.com; press releases; public videos, calls, and webcasts; and social media: X (@exodus and JP Richardson’s feed @jprichardson), Facebook, LinkedIn, and YouTube. title: How to Open a Dispensary in Minnesota: A 2026 Guide
summary: How to open a dispensary in Minnesota in 2026: license types, the lottery, social equity, costs, and compliance. A first-mover guide for new operators.
body_text: Minnesota's adult-use cannabis market launched on September 16, 2025, and it is moving fast. By April 2026, approximately 148 licensed dispensaries were operating statewide, monthly sales hit a record $22 million in March 2026, and MJBizDaily projects full-year 2026 adult-use sales could reach $430 million. The market is still early, supply is tighter than demand, and new licenses are still being awarded. Operators who move now and build compliant operations from day one have a genuine edge. Because the market is still settling under the Office of Cannabis Management (OCM), the rules, fees, and timelines keep evolving. Whether you're a legacy operator or new to the space, this guide walks you through what it takes to open a licensed dispensary in Minnesota in 2026: licensing, inspections, operational readiness, and launch. Always confirm current details with the OCM before acting. In This Post Understand Minnesota Cannabis Licensing Requirements Develop a Robust Security Plan, Store Layout, and SOPs Choose a Cannabis POS Built for Minnesota Compliance Hire and Train a High-Performing Team Launch Your Website Streamline Operations with API Integrations Set Your Dispensary Up for Long-Term Success in Minnesota Common Questions Opening a Minnesota Dispensary? Talk to the Team. Understand Minnesota Cannabis Licensing Requirements To open a dispensary in Minnesota, you need to meet several critical requirements: the right license, Metrc seed-to-sale compliance, municipal approvals, and a passed OCM inspection. These are the foundational steps that get you compliant and open. Who Regulates Cannabis in Minnesota Minnesota legalized adult-use cannabis in 2023. The Office of Cannabis Management (OCM) handles licensing, rules, inspections, and enforcement. (Minnesota shares the "OCM" acronym with New York's regulator, but they're entirely separate agencies with different rules. Don't assume one state's process maps to the other.) License Types Minnesota uses a tiered license structure spanning cultivation through retail. For storefront operators, the key tiers are the Cannabis Retailer , Cannabis Microbusiness , and Cannabis Mezzobusiness licenses. Caps matter: the Cannabis Microbusiness license is uncapped, while the Cannabis Mezzobusiness and standalone Cannabis Retailer licenses are capped and awarded by lottery. Under Minnesota statute, OCM is required to review whether the number of available licenses is consistent with statutory goals beginning July 1, 2026, which could affect caps going forward. Study the Cannabis Retailer tier first and confirm the current list of license types, caps, and any pending cap adjustments with the OCM. Social Equity Applicants Minnesota built social equity into its rollout from the start, giving qualifying applicants priority access, including earlier application windows and preference in capped-license lotteries. If you may qualify, confirm the criteria early. It can materially change your timeline and your odds. The Application and Lottery Process For capped license types, Minnesota uses a lottery among qualified applicants. The licensing process runs in distinct phases: application submission, qualification review, lottery (for capped types), preliminary approval, Final Plan of Record (FPOR) submission, local certification, inspection, and final license issuance. Key things to plan for: Confirm the open window and whether your license type is lottery-based or first-come. Form your business entity and assemble ownership disclosures. Meet pre-application requirements: financing, an operating plan, and social-equity verification if applicable. Submit during the window and pay the fees. If selected , note that preliminary approval is not a license to operate. You have up to 18 months (with a possible six-month extension for demonstrated good-faith progress) to convert preliminary approval into full licensure by completing your FPOR and passing inspection. The rollout has a contested history: an earlier social-equity preapproval lottery planned for November 2024 was canceled, then a court in April 2025 ordered the OCM to proceed. Treat any date you read elsewhere as provisional and verify with the OCM directly. Location Rules Expect local zoning and registration requirements on top of your state license. Minnesota law requires dispensaries to be at least 500 feet from schools, public parks, and libraries, and sited in areas zoned for commercial or industrial use. Minnesota also gives municipalities a defined role, and local approval can be the gating step. Don't sign a lease before confirming the site qualifies under both state and local rules. Note that as of writing, legislation (SF 4401) was advancing that would set a statewide minimum floor on local retail access. Confirm current local requirements before you commit to a location. Costs and Timeline Budget for application and licensing fees , plus real opening costs: build-out, real estate, security, inventory, staffing, and working capital. Fees are still evolving, so pull current numbers from the OCM rather than relying on older figures. Timelines depend on license type and lottery rounds, but plan for months from application to opening, and up to 18 months from preliminary approval to full licensure. Remember that federal 280E disallows most operating-expense deductions, so plan your cash and tax reserves accordingly. Compliance with Metrc and State Regulations Once you have conditional approval, compliance becomes your most important ongoing operational discipline. Minnesota uses Metrc as its official seed-to-sale tracking system. Every cannabis product must be tracked from arrival to sale or destruction. Here's what that means in practice: Track-and-trace inventory: Every product must be linked to a Metrc package tag. Sales must be accurately reported and packages depleted correctly to avoid discrepancies. Sales limits and customer verification: You're responsible for enforcing purchase limits and verifying legal age. Your POS should handle these checks automatically at check-in and point of sale. Staff training: Everyone handling cannabis must understand Metrc and follow state protocols. Build Metrc training into your onboarding process from day one. Background checks: As of March 1, 2026, all cannabis businesses and prospective employees who have not yet completed a background check must do so through the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension (BCA) process. Build BCA processing time into your staffing and onboarding plans. New to Inventory Management? Download our Guidebook Compliance isn't a one-time setup. It's an ongoing operational discipline, and the right tools and routines keep you out of trouble when inspectors come calling. Develop a Robust Security Plan, Store Layout, and SOPs To operate a cannabis dispensary in Minnesota, you'll need a comprehensive security plan that protects your staff, customers, and inventory while meeting OCM and local law enforcement expectations. Set up compliant check-in procedures with tools that verify customer age, create profiles, and keep your front-of-house secure. Security Plan Requirements A well-developed dispensary security plan isn't just a compliance requirement. It's a critical tool to protect your team, your customers, and your investment. Your written security plan will be reviewed during licensing and inspection. At minimum, it should address: Surveillance and intrusion detection: 24/7 video coverage across all sensitive areas with monitored alarm systems and documented emergency response protocols. Secure inventory and access control: Cannabis products stored in locked, access-restricted areas with systems tracking who enters inventory zones. Incident protocols and reporting: Clear SOPs for documenting and reporting theft, loss, or suspicious activity per OCM regulations. Read more: How to Build a Dispensary Security Plan: 7 Expert Strategies Store Layout Considerations The best floor plans are built for compliance, efficiency, and security, not just aesthetics. Consider: Clear entry and check-in zone: Customers are greeted in a designated area where IDs are verified before they access the sales floor. Secure fulfillment area: Inventory stays away from high-traffic areas, with access limited to trained staff. Smooth traffic flow: A sales floor that avoids bottlenecks, accommodates foot traffic, and supports accessibility. Surveillance visibility: Clear camera views with nothing blocking coverage zones. Thoughtful store design, product placement, and customer flow all contribute to a successful dispensary shopping experience. A well-designed store layout, paired with a strong security plan, will help you pass inspections, protect your team, and create a safe, welcoming environment for your customers. Read more: Choosing the Best Sales Model for Cannabis Retail Success Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) SOPs are how you maintain consistency, safety, and compliance across every shift. Whether it's opening, closing, receiving inventory, or handling an incident, clear written procedures keep your team aligned and your operation inspection-ready. Read more: Cannabis Dispensary Opening Checklist | Closing Checklist Choose a Cannabis POS Built for Minnesota Compliance Your point of sale is the operational backbone of your dispensary. From ringing up customers to managing inventory, syncing with Metrc, and enforcing purchase limits, your POS needs to keep you audit-ready and running efficiently from day one. As you prepare to launch in Minnesota, look for a system purpose-built for cannabis retail that aligns with OCM regulations and supports your specific store workflows. Equip your team with a cannabis-specific POS that makes it easy to build carts, track inventory, and stay compliant. Key Features to Look For in Cannabis POS Software Metrc integration: Real-time sync with Metrc is non-negotiable. It keeps inventory accurate, automates sales reporting, and prevents issues like ghost inventory or negative balances. Support for diverse retail workflows: Your POS should adapt to your in-store model, whether that's quick counter service, guided consultations, or fulfillment-first operations, all from one integrated platform. Inventory management tools: Built-in receiving, labeling, cycle counts, and audit logs keep inventory in sync and compliance issues from compounding. Live eCommerce menu: Your online menu should reflect current inventory in real time and provide a seamless experience for customers ordering ahead or browsing from home. Built-in text marketing: Drive repeat visits by sending targeted SMS campaigns directly from your POS. No third-party tool required. Loyalty and CRM capabilities: Retain customers with rewards, automated promos, and personalized outreach. Actionable reporting and insights: Sales, product, and staff performance data should be easy to pull and act on, so you make faster, smarter decisions. Uptime and support: A reliable system with responsive support means your team has what it needs during peak hours and inspections. Staff training tools: Intuitive onboarding and guided resources get new hires up to speed fast without pulling experienced staff off the floor. Since 2014, Meadow has helped dispensaries navigate compliance, scale operations, and serve their communities. Whether you're opening your first store or expanding into Minnesota's new market, our platform and team are here to help you launch with confidence. Read more: The Complete Guide to Choosing a Cannabis Dispensary POS System Hire and Train a High-Performing Team Your dispensary's success depends on the strength of your team. From budtenders to inventory managers, each role plays a critical part in compliance, customer service, and day-to-day operations. Train your team to offer product education and support, while keeping conversations compliant with Minnesota's cannabis regulations. Key Roles to Fill Hire for core positions including: Budtenders who can educate customers and stay compliant with age and purchase limits Inventory Managers who maintain Metrc accuracy and oversee receiving, tagging, and reconciliation Store Managers who lead the team, manage daily operations, and serve as the main point of contact for regulators Set user permissions based on role to protect your data, streamline access, and ensure each team member has the tools they need without risking compliance or security. Read more: Budtender Training Best Practices for Your Dispensary Launch Your Website A real-time online menu is the foundation of any cannabis retail business. Here's what to look for when choosing and setting one up. Live inventory sync. Your menu should update automatically the moment a product is sold, restocked, or repriced, across your website, Weedmaps, Leafly, and any pickup channels. A menu that shows out-of-stock products loses customer trust and creates manual work. Mobile-first design. Most cannabis customers browse and order from their phones. Choose a menu solution that loads fast, looks clean on mobile, and makes checkout simple. Page speed affects both conversion and search ranking. Built-in SEO. Your online menu should generate unique URLs for every product and category page, not load everything through a single iframe. Unique URLs are indexable by search engines and help customers find specific products directly from Google. Easy integration. Look for a menu that connects to your POS without custom dev work, ideally a single line of code, and syncs inventory automatically so you're not manually managing multiple listings. 💡 How Meadow handles this: Meadow's Menu Pro keeps every menu in sync in real time across all channels, generates unique SEO-friendly URLs for every product page, and deploys with one line of code. See how Menu Pro works Read more: How to Create a Great Cannabis eCommerce Shopping Experience Streamline Operations with API Integrations As your dispensary grows, your tech stack will expand beyond POS and ecommerce. API integrations let your tools, payments, CRM, marketing, and accounting, talk to each other in real time, eliminating duplicate work and manual data entry. Common dispensary integrations include compliant payments (PIN debit, ACH, digital), marketing and SMS platforms that trigger off purchase behavior, and accounting tools like QuickBooks to speed reconciliation and tax prep. Operators who invest in connected systems early are best positioned to thrive as Minnesota's market matures. A seamless front-of-house experience depends on well-integrated tools that connect POS, inventory, payments, and customer data in real time. Check out Meadow's API Integration Partners . Set Your Dispensary Up for Long-Term Success in Minnesota Creating a welcoming, educational shopping experience builds trust and drives long-term customer loyalty, key to sustained success in a new market. Opening a dispensary in Minnesota requires careful planning, the right partners, and a clear understanding of the state's evolving regulations. From building your team and setting up your store to implementing Metrc and selecting compliant tech, every decision you make now shapes the strength and sustainability of your operation. Operators who build smart systems, train staff thoroughly, and design thoughtful workflows will be better equipped to meet compliance standards, serve their customers, and grow over time. We know what it takes to go from license to launch, and how to keep things running smoothly as you scale. If you're getting ready to open your doors in Minnesota, we're here to help. Common Questions How do I get a dispensary license in Minnesota? For capped license types, the Cannabis Mezzobusiness and standalone Cannabis Retailer, Minnesota awards licenses by lottery among qualified applicants, with priority for verified social equity applicants. The Cannabis Microbusiness license is uncapped. Form your entity, prepare ownership and financing disclosures, and submit during an open window. If selected, you'll have up to 18 months to convert preliminary approval into full licensure. Always confirm current requirements and windows with the OCM. When did Minnesota dispensaries open? Adult-use retail sales launched on September 16, 2025, following the state's first license lotteries in mid-2025. As of April 2026, approximately 148 licensed dispensaries were operating statewide, with new locations continuing to open each month. Does Minnesota use Metrc? Yes. Minnesota uses Metrc as its official seed-to-sale tracking system. Every product must be tracked from arrival to sale or destruction, and your POS should sync with Metrc in real time. How much does it cost to open a dispensary in Minnesota? Plan for application and licensing fees plus real opening costs: build-out, real estate, security, inventory, staffing, and working capital. Fees are still evolving, so confirm current amounts with the OCM and budget for federal 280E tax exposure. What is the 18-month preliminary approval deadline? After winning a lottery and receiving preliminary approval, Minnesota operators have up to 18 months to complete their Final Plan of Record, pass inspection, and obtain a full license. A one-time six-month extension may be available if you can demonstrate good-faith progress. This is one of the most important regulatory deadlines to track. What background check does Minnesota require for dispensary staff? title: Sonic Automotive Opens New Massey Cadillac of South Orlando Dealership in Lake Nona
body_text: Sonic Automotive Opens New Massey Cadillac of South Orlando Dealership in Lake Nona Download as PDF July 27, 2026 • 11:00am EDT Strategic Relocation Brings Expanded Capabilities and a Modern Luxury Experience to Central Florida CHARLOTTE, N.C., July 27, 2026 – Sonic Automotive, Inc. ( NYSE: SAH ), one of the nation’s largest automotive and powersports retailers and a recipient of Newsweek’s 2026 “Most Trustworthy Companies in America” award, has officially announced the relocation of its Massey Cadillac of South Orlando dealership to the high-growth Lake Nona community. The new 34,000-square-foot facility, located at 2698 J Lawson Blvd, is now fully operational. The relocation reflects Sonic Automotive’s continued commitment to the Cadillac brand and its evolving portfolio of luxury vehicles. The new custom facility brings a modern showroom, advanced digital retail tools, and a significantly expanded service capability to the region, featuring 17 service bays equipped to maintain and repair Cadillac’s full vehicle lineup, including dedicated infrastructure for electric vehicle service. As the largest Cadillac dealer in Central Florida and a top ten Cadillac EV retailer in the nation, Massey Cadillac of South Orlando is uniquely positioned to help guests navigate the future of luxury mobility. Massey Cadillac of South Orlando complements Sonic’s Massey Cadillac of North Orlando dealership, and together, these dealerships offer the largest inventory of Cadillac vehicles in the Orlando community. These dealerships, along with nine other automotive and powersports dealerships owned by Sonic Automotive throughout Florida, provide guests with high-quality inventory and world-class sales and service experience. “We’ve been serving the Orlando community since 2002, and are proud to bring the Massey Cadillac of South Orlando experience to a new home in Lake Nona,” said David B. Smith, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Sonic Automotive, Inc. “This new, state-of-the-art facility reflects our commitment to the Cadillac brand, offering a premium environment for our guests to shop and advanced tools for our teammates to service today’s vehicles and the next generation of Cadillac products. Combined with our Massey Cadillac of North Orlando dealership, we’re proud to provide access to the largest Cadillac inventory in Central Florida.” Massey Cadillac of South Orlando was named a 2025 Cadillac Dealer of the Year, an award given to the top 20 dealerships nationwide in recognition of excellence in sales, service, and the overall ownership experience. This relocation marks an exciting new chapter while preserving the trusted relationships and personalized service that have defined the dealership’s role in the community for generations. The new Massey Cadillac of South Orlando dealership in Lake Nona is now open to the public. For operating hours, service appointments and to view our current inventory, visit masseycadillacsouth.com . About Massey Cadillac of South Orlando Massey Cadillac of South Orlando is a premier Cadillac retailer serving Central Florida. Known for delivering exceptional luxury automotive sales and service experiences, the dealership was awarded the 2025 Cadillac Dealer of the Year award and is one of the top ten Cadillac EV retailers in the nation. Massey Cadillac of South Orlando offers guests access to the largest Cadillac inventory across its Central Florida locations while providing expert guidance throughout every stage of vehicle ownership. Find out more at masseycadillacsouth.com . About Sonic Automotive For more than 60 years, Sonic Automotive has pursued a single purpose: to deliver an experience for our guests and our teammates that fulfills dreams, enriches lives, and delivers happiness. We don’t simply sell and service vehicles. We help people pursue their dreams, whether it’s a guest purchasing their first vehicle, a family creating lifelong memories, or a teammate building a meaningful career. Founded in 1966 by Bruton Smith, the company has grown into a Fortune 300 company under the leadership of Chairman and CEO David B. Smith. Today, more than 11,000 teammates bring the company’s purpose to life across a nationwide network of 173 automotive and powersports franchises in 145 locations in 90 cities and 21 states. We are proud to represent 24 automotive and 15 powersports brands and have helped more than 7 million guests purchase vehicles, delivered over 40 million service experiences, and earned more than 1 million 5-star reviews by consistently putting people first. At Sonic Automotive, we believe trust isn’t claimed – it’s earned through transparency, consistency, integrity, and genuine care. That’s why we were the only automotive and powersports retailer recognized by Newsweek as one of America’s Most Trustworthy Companies in 2026. As the automotive and powersports industries continue to evolve, our mission remains constant: to innovate, lead with integrity, and create exceptional experiences that inspire confidence, build lifelong relationships, and positively impact every life we touch. Sonic Automotive. Driven By People. Inspired By Purpose. For more information, visit www.sonicautomotive.com and ir.sonicautomotive.com . Sonic Automotive Press Inquiries Sonic Automotive Media Relations media.relations@sonicautomotive.com Released July 27, 2026

title: How Long Does Background Verification Take in India? Realistic Timelines for Every Type of Check
summary: How long does employee background verification take in India? Learn exact timelines for identity, education, and criminal checks, plus how to speed up hiring.
body_text: Insights & Resources How Long Does Background Verification Take in India? Realistic Timelines for Every Type of Check July 31, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet If you have ever made a job offer and then waited anxiously for the background verification to come through, you know how frustrating the uncertainty can be. The candidate is eager to start. Your team needs the position filled. And somewhere in the process, someone is waiting for a university to respond to an email or for court records to be pulled from a dusty archive. Background verification in India can take anywhere from a few minutes to several weeks, depending on what checks you run and how you run them. The difference between the fastest and slowest approaches is enormous, and most employers have no idea that faster, more affordable options exist. In this guide, we will break down exactly how long each type of background check takes in India, what causes delays, and how you can dramatically speed up the process without compromising on quality. The Short Answer A basic digital identity verification takes minutes. A standard multi check background verification takes 3 to 7 business days. A comprehensive verification that includes physical address checks and court record searches can take 7 to 15 business days. And a complex case involving multiple states, unresponsive previous employers, or manual court searches can stretch to 20 business days or more. The wide range exists because “background verification” is not a single check. It is a combination of several different checks, each with its own timeline. Let us look at each one individually. Timeline Breakdown by Check Type Identity Verification: Minutes to 24 Hours This is the fastest type of background check, and it is also the most fundamental. Identity verification confirms that a person is who they claim to be by checking their government issued documents against official databases. PAN Card Verification takes seconds to minutes when done digitally. The PAN number is checked against the Income Tax Department database to verify the name, date of birth, and PAN status. This is an instant API based check. Voter ID Verification is similarly quick. The EPIC number is validated against the Election Commission of India database, confirming the person’s identity and registered address. This check typically completes in under a minute. Driving Licence Verification checks the DL number against the VAHAN/SARATHI database maintained by the Ministry of Road Transport. This is also a near instant digital check that confirms the licence holder’s name, date of birth, and licence validity. UAN Verification checks the Universal Account Number against EPFO records. This reveals employment history including previous employer names, joining and leaving dates, and PF contribution patterns. This check can take anywhere from a few minutes to 24 hours depending on the platform. The key insight here is that identity verification has become almost entirely digital in India. If you are still waiting days for identity checks, you are using an outdated process. Platforms like ID Verify by SalaryBox (verify.salarybox.in) run PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, and UAN checks in real time against government databases. You get results in minutes, not days. Education Verification: 3 to 15 Business Days This is where things start to slow down. Education verification involves contacting the university, college, or educational board that issued the candidate’s degree or diploma to confirm that the qualification is genuine. The timeline depends heavily on the institution. Universities that have digitised their records and have a dedicated verification cell can respond in 3 to 5 business days. Institutions that still rely on manual record retrieval, especially older universities and state boards, can take 10 to 15 business days or even longer. The National Academic Depository (NAD) was created to solve this problem by providing a digital repository of academic records. However, adoption is still not universal, and many institutions have not uploaded their records to NAD. What causes delays: Multiple follow ups needed with the institution. University is on semester break or has limited staff. Records are stored in physical archives. The institution has no formal verification process. How to speed it up: Use a verification service that has existing relationships with major universities. Check if the institution’s records are available on NAD first. Start education verification early in the hiring process rather than waiting until the offer stage. Employment Verification: 3 to 10 Business Days Employment verification confirms that the candidate actually worked at the companies they claim on their resume. It typically involves contacting the HR department of each previous employer to verify job title, dates of employment, and sometimes reason for leaving. The timeline is unpredictable because it depends entirely on how responsive the previous employer is. Large companies with dedicated HR teams usually respond within 3 to 5 business days. Smaller companies or startups that have shut down may not respond at all. What causes delays: Previous employer’s HR team is slow to respond. The company has been acquired, merged, or shut down. The candidate worked at a very small company with no formal HR function. Contact details for the previous employer are incorrect. How to speed it up: UAN verification through EPFO records is a powerful shortcut. When you verify a candidate’s UAN, you can see their actual PF contribution history, which shows the names of employers, contribution dates, and employment duration. This gives you an independent, government sourced record of employment history without needing to contact any previous employer. ID Verify by SalaryBox includes UAN verification as one of its standard checks, giving you employment history data in minutes rather than the days or weeks it takes to get responses from previous employers. Criminal Record Check: 7 to 14 Business Days Criminal record verification is one of the most important checks and unfortunately one of the slowest. India does not have a centralised criminal database that covers all jurisdictions. This means criminal record checks require searching court records across multiple districts and states. Digital court record checks through the eCourts database can be completed in 3 to 7 business days. The eCourts system covers most district courts and high courts, and searches can be conducted by name and other identifying details. Physical court record checks are needed when digital records are not available or when a more thorough search is required. These involve sending a representative to physically check records at specific courts. This can take 10 to 14 business days or longer, especially for smaller courts in rural areas. Police verification is a separate process where the local police conduct their own check on the candidate. The timeline varies dramatically by state and district. In some areas it takes a week. In others it can take a month or more. What causes delays: Multiple jurisdictions need to be searched. Court records are not digitised. Common names produce many results that need manual review. The candidate has lived in multiple states. Police verification backlogs in certain areas. How to speed it up: Start with digital court record searches to catch any obvious issues quickly. Combine this with identity verification to ensure you are searching for the right person. If you need police verification, submit the request early and do not wait for other checks to complete first. Address Verification: 1 to 7 Business Days Address verification confirms that the candidate actually lives at the address they have provided. This can be done digitally or through a physical visit. Digital address verification uses database checks and can be completed in 1 to 2 business days. It cross references the address against electoral rolls, utility connections, and other databases. Physical address verification involves sending a field agent to the address to confirm the candidate’s residence. This takes 3 to 7 business days and is more thorough because the agent can also talk to neighbours and verify the living situation. What causes delays: Candidate lives in a remote or hard to reach area. Candidate has recently moved and address records have not been updated. The person at the address is not available when the field agent visits. Drug Test: 1 to 3 Business Days If your company requires pre employment drug testing, the timeline is relatively straightforward. The candidate visits a designated collection centre, provides a sample, and results are typically available within 1 to 3 business days. Credit Check: 1 to 3 Business Days Credit checks are typically required only for roles that involve financial responsibilities. These checks are conducted through credit bureaus like CIBIL, Experian, or Equifax, and results are usually available within 1 to 3 business days. Total Timeline: Putting It All Together Here is what a typical background verification timeline looks like when all checks run in parallel. Basic verification (identity only): Same day. If you only need to verify that a candidate’s identity documents are genuine, you can get this done in minutes through digital verification. Standard verification (identity plus employment plus education): 5 to 10 business days. Identity checks complete almost instantly, but you will be waiting on education and employment verification responses. Comprehensive verification (all checks): 10 to 15 business days. This includes criminal record searches and address verification, which add to the timeline. Complex cases: 15 to 20+ business days. If the candidate has lived in multiple states, worked at companies that are hard to reach, or attended institutions with poor record keeping, expect the process to stretch. Why Traditional Background Verification Takes So Long The traditional approach to background verification in India is built on a model that was designed decades ago. Here is why it is slow. Manual processes. Many verification agencies still rely on phone calls, emails, and physical document collection. Each interaction requires waiting for a response, and follow ups add more time. Fragmented databases. India does not have unified national databases for criminal records, education credentials, or employment history. Each check requires reaching out to a different source, and each source has its own response timeline. Volume bottlenecks. Popular verification agencies handle thousands of requests simultaneously. During peak hiring seasons, backlogs build up and turnaround times increase. Intermediary chains. Large verification agencies often subcontract field checks to local agents, adding another layer of communication and potential delays. How to Dramatically Speed Up Your Background Verification Process The biggest time saving opportunity is in the checks you can control. And the good news is that the most important check, identity verification, is also the fastest. Prioritize Digital Identity Verification Instead of waiting for a comprehensive background verification package to complete, run digital identity checks first. This gives you immediate confirmation of the candidate’s identity and catches the most common issues right away. When someone submits a fake PAN card, a forged Voter ID, or a Driving Licence with mismatched details, digital verification catches it in minutes. You do not need to wait weeks for a field agent to discover the same thing. Use UAN as an Employment Verification Shortcut Traditional employment verification involves calling previous employers and waiting for callbacks. UAN verification gives you government sourced employment history data almost instantly. When you check a candidate’s UAN through EPFO, you can see every employer who contributed to their PF account, when contributions started and stopped, and the contribution amounts. This is independent, tamper proof data that is far more reliable than a verbal confirmation from an HR department. Run Checks in Parallel, Not Sequentially Many companies make the mistake of running background checks one after another. They wait for identity verification to complete before starting education verification, then wait for that before starting employment checks. Run everything in parallel. Submit all check requests on the same day. This way, your total turnaround time equals the time of the slowest check, not the sum of all checks. Start Verification Before the Offer If background verification consistently delays your hiring, consider starting basic checks earlier in the process. Running identity verification during the interview stage costs very little and can eliminate candidates with fake credentials before you invest time in further interviews and salary negotiations. The Case for Starting with Identity Verification Here is a practical approach that many smart hiring teams in India have adopted. Run digital identity verification on shortlisted candidates before making an offer. This takes minutes and costs very little per check. It catches the most common forms of fraud immediately. Then, after the offer is accepted, run the remaining checks like education verification, criminal record search, and address verification. Let the candidate start work on a provisional basis while these checks complete. This approach reduces your time to hire by days or even weeks while still maintaining a thorough verification process. And because identity verification catches the majority of document fraud, you are not taking a significant risk by letting someone start before the slower checks finish. ID Verify by SalaryBox (verify.salarybox.in) is built exactly for this workflow. You can run PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, and UAN checks on demand, one candidate at a time, without any subscription or minimum order. The pay per check pricing means you only spend money on the checks you actually need. What Happens When Background Verification Gets Delayed? Delays in background verification create real problems for both employers and candidates. Candidates drop out. In a competitive job market, good candidates do not wait around. If your verification process takes three weeks, the candidate may accept another offer from a company with a faster process. Studies suggest that 30 to 40 percent of candidates drop out during lengthy verification processes. Projects get delayed. Every day a position remains unfilled costs the company in lost productivity. If you are hiring for a critical role, a two week verification delay translates directly into business impact. Candidate experience suffers. Even candidates who wait through a long verification process start their new job with a negative impression. They feel like the company does not respect their time or does not have efficient processes. Costs increase. Extended verification timelines mean more follow ups, more administrative work, and sometimes the need to restart the hiring process when candidates drop out. Industry Specific Timelines Different industries face different verification challenges and timelines. IT and technology companies typically complete verification in 5 to 7 business days because most checks can be done digitally and candidates generally have well documented educational and employment histories. Banking and financial services (BFSI) require more thorough checks including credit history and criminal records, which extends the timeline to 10 to 15 business days. Regulatory requirements in this sector make shortcuts difficult. Healthcare verification can take 10 to 14 business days because medical credentials need to be verified with specific medical councils and registration bodies, which can be slow to respond. Manufacturing and blue collar hiring often has the fastest turnaround because the verification focus is primarily on identity and address, both of which can be completed quickly. Digital identity verification makes this even faster. Retail and hospitality companies that hire in volume often need verification completed within 3 to 5 days to meet seasonal demand. Digital identity verification platforms are particularly valuable for these industries. Frequently Asked Questions Can background verification be done in one day? Basic identity verification can absolutely be done in one day, often in just minutes. A full comprehensive background check including education, employment, criminal records, and address verification cannot realistically be completed in one day because it depends on external parties responding to verification requests. What is the fastest type of background check in India? Digital identity verification is the fastest. PAN verification, Voter ID verification, and Driving Licence verification can be completed in seconds to minutes through API based checks against government databases. UAN verification, which provides employment history, is also very fast. Why does my company’s background verification take so long? Common reasons include running checks sequentially instead of in parallel, using a vendor that relies on manual processes, ordering checks that are not relevant to the role, and not following up proactively with verification sources. Switching to a platform that offers digital verification for identity checks can significantly reduce your overall timeline. Can a candidate start work before background verification is complete? Yes, many companies allow candidates to start on a provisional basis while slower checks like education and criminal record verification are pending. The key is to complete identity verification before the start date so you know the person is who they claim to be. Make the offer letter conditional on satisfactory completion of all background checks. What should I do if background verification reveals a discrepancy? Not all discrepancies are deal breakers. A minor spelling variation in a name across documents could be a data entry error. Give the candidate a chance to explain any discrepancies before making a decision. However, if the discrepancy involves a completely different identity, a fake degree, or a concealed criminal record, those are serious issues that typically warrant rescinding the offer. How much does fast background verification cost in India? Digital identity verification through platforms like ID Verify by SalaryBox costs just a few rupees per check. This is dramatically less than traditional verification agencies that charge Rs 1,500 to Rs 5,000 per candidate for a comprehensive package. The digital approach is not only faster but also significantly more affordable. Stop Waiting. Start Verifying. The era of waiting weeks for background verification results is over. title: Rhode Island Energy Announces Operations Leadership Appointments
summary: PROVIDENCE, R.I. (July 7, 2026) – Rhode Island Energy (RIE) today announced two leadership appointments within its Operations organization, strengthening the company’s continued focus on...
body_text: PROVIDENCE, R.I. ( July 7, 2026 ) – Rhode Island Energy (RIE) today announced two leadership appointments within its Operations organization, strengthening the company’s continued focus on safety, reliability, and operational performance for customers across the Ocean State. Michele Leone, currently Vice President of Gas Operations, has been named Chief Operations Officer of Rhode Island. She succeeds Al LaBarre, who will retire effective August 1 after 38 years of service with the company. Leone brings more than 26 years of experience in the New England utility industry, with leadership roles spanning gas, electric, environmental, and sustainability operations. In her new role, she will oversee electric and gas operations across Rhode Island, focusing on improving performance, strengthening cross-functional coordination, and maintaining a strong commitment to safety and reliability. “Michele’s deep experience and proven leadership make her exceptionally well-suited to lead our operations in Rhode Island,” said Greg Cornett, President of Rhode Island Energy. “Following Al’s many years of dedicated service, Michele is well positioned to build on that strong foundation as we continue delivering safe, reliable energy for our customers and communities.” Leone holds a Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering from Syracuse University and a Master of Science in Environmental Engineering from the University of Michigan at Ann Arbor. She is a graduate of the 2016 Leadership Rhode Island Core Program and has served on the Leadership Rhode Island Board of Governors since 2018. In addition, Kathy Castro, currently Vice President of Electric Distribution Operations, has been appointed Vice President of Gas Operations. Castro brings 23 years of utility experience in the New England region, with leadership roles across engineering, asset management, distribution planning, customer project development, field operations, and regulatory strategy. She is known for her collaborative leadership style, strong focus on safety and reliability, and commitment to developing teams. “Kathy brings a wealth of operational experience and a collaborative approach that will serve our gas business, customers, and communities well,” Cornett added. “She has consistently championed safety, reliability, and strong performance while helping drive the work needed to build a stronger, more resilient energy future.” Castro holds a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and a Graduate Certificate in Power Systems Management from Worcester Polytechnic Institute. A selection process to fill the role of Vice President of Electric Operations will take place in the coming weeks. About Rhode Island Energy Rhode Island Energy provides essential energy services to over 770,000 customers across Rhode Island through the delivery of electricity and natural gas. Our team of more than 1,300 employees is dedicated to helping Rhode Island customers and communities thrive, while supporting the transition to a cleaner energy future. Rhode Island Energy is part of the PPL Corporation (NYSE: PPL) family of companies addressing energy challenges head-on by building smarter, more resilient, and more dynamic power grids and advancing sustainable energy solutions. For more information visit www.RIEnergy.com and stay connected on Instagram , LinkedIn , Facebook , and X .

title: What Is an AM Best Rating? A Startup Founder's Guide
summary: What an AM Best rating means, why enterprise vendors require A-rated carriers, and the 6 mistakes founders make when buying insurance from non-rated companies.
body_text: What is the minimum A.M. Best rating most vendor contracts require? Most Fortune 500 and enterprise vendor contracts require A- (Excellent) or better. Federal government contracts and regulated industries (banking, healthcare, defense) often require A (Excellent) or A+ (Superior). Always check the insurance exhibit in your specific contract — it will state the requirement explicitly if one exists. Can a non-rated carrier ever be acceptable? Occasionally, for very specific coverage types in niche markets where rated capacity doesn't exist. But for standard startup lines — General Liability, Tech E&O, Cyber, D&O — there is no reason to accept a non-rated carrier. Rated options are available at competitive prices in all of these lines. What happens if my carrier's rating drops during my policy term? Your coverage remains in force — a downgrade doesn't void the policy. But your vendor contract may require you to maintain coverage with a carrier meeting the stated threshold, which could mean re-placing coverage mid-term if the carrier drops below it. Your broker should notify you of material rating changes. Is a surplus lines carrier always lower quality than an admitted carrier? No. Many of the strongest carriers in specialty lines operate as surplus lines (non-admitted) carriers because certain risks don't fit standard admitted markets. A surplus lines carrier with an A.M. Best A rating is financially stronger than an admitted carrier with a B+ rating. The admitted/non-admitted distinction affects state regulation and guarantee-fund protection — not necessarily financial strength. What does "admitted" mean on a certificate of insurance? A COI doesn't typically state whether a carrier is admitted or non-admitted — that's on the policy declarations page. If a contract requires an admitted carrier specifically, ask your broker to confirm the carrier's admitted status in your state before binding.
